binding_from: the git commit that adds this file -- that commit must precede any NQ dense episode run on the test population below
reason: The paper's dense-retrieval check ('Does this hold under dense retrieval?', Section 4) is TripClick-only, and there the paired AUC-difference CI does not exclude zero ([-0.004,+0.083]). A second-corpus dense replication on BEIR NQ tests whether that null-ish result is TripClick-specific. Its test scope is fixed here, before any NQ dense episode exists, so the scope cannot be chosen after seeing an outcome.

fit.use: every model fit, CV diagnostic, and any smoke test

frozen_test.source: scripts/25_nq_test_extension.py extension_qids() -- full 3,452-query NQ pool minus nq_split.json val[800] and test[600]

excluded.use: never run under dense retrieval, not as primary, secondary, or pooled. Running it too would create a choice of which dense test number to report.

scope_rationale: Parity with the paper's main NQ result, which reports this same 2,052-query confirmatory set, unpooled with the 600 pilot (paper Section 3; Table 1's n=2,013 is its acted-upon subset).
Parity with the TripClick dense check's own standard: the same query population as the BM25 headline (full TAIL test, n=1175), not a subset.
The n=600 pool is already documented as underpowered for this AUC comparison (configs/nq_test_extension_precommit.json: action-utility CI [0.442,0.602]).
Status of these queries: touched once by the frozen BM25 pipeline, never by any dense pipeline -- the same status TripClick TAIL test had when its dense check ran.

frozen_pipeline.retriever: BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, float16 memmap, full BEIR NQ corpus (2,681,468 docs), built by scripts/41 into data/nq_dense_{meta.sqlite3,embeddings.f16,ids.txt}
frozen_pipeline.telemetry: scripts/33 reduced telemetry set, unchanged (same features as the TripClick dense check)
frozen_pipeline.episode_logic: scripts/35 run_episode(), unchanged, pointed at the NQ dense index and NQ qrels
frozen_pipeline.detection_label: y_poor = 1 iff the dense retriever's original nDCG@10 <= 1e-9 (zero relevant in its own top 10), as in scripts/35
frozen_pipeline.action_utility_label: delta_ndcg < -1e-9, acted-upon episodes only (those with au_features), as in scripts/35/36
frozen_pipeline.models: LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000), sklearn defaults otherwise, for both tasks; fit once on all val episodes. No GBDT and no model sweep -- scripts/37/42's non-linear findings stay validation-only, consistent with the paper not adopting them.
frozen_pipeline.val_diagnostic: detection 5-fold StratifiedKFold CV AUC (shuffle, seed 42) on val, reported and labeled as validation-only, never as the result

reported_statistics.primary: test detection AUC and test action-utility AUC, each with a 95% percentile bootstrap CI (10,000 resamples, seed 42), plus the AUC difference (detection minus action-utility) and its 95% CI from a true paired bootstrap per scripts/28: both AUCs evaluated on the acted-upon test subset, and each resample of those queries recomputes BOTH AUCs on the same resampled indices (resamples with a single class in either label skipped).
reported_statistics.difference_ci_note: Deliberately NOT scripts/36's procedure, which holds detection AUC fixed on the full test set and resamples only the action-utility side -- that is not paired and understates the difference's variance. The TripClick dense difference CI will be recomputed with this same scripts/28 method from the saved results/dense_retrieval_full_scale_raw.json (existing records, existing val-fit models, no new test touch) so both dense rows in the paper use one correct procedure.
also_reported: dense pre-action failure rate on test
dense mean nDCG@10 on test vs. frozen NQ BM25 on the same 2,052 queries (the retriever-strength confound the TripClick paragraph checks)
reported_statistics.interpretation_rule: 'Reproduces the asymmetry under dense retrieval on NQ' iff the difference CI's lower bound > 0 with detection > action-utility. Any other outcome is reported as not significantly reproducing it, in the same wording style as the TripClick dense paragraph.
reported_statistics.reporting_commitment: Reported in full regardless of outcome, including if it weakens the paper's claim.

run_rules: Val episodes run to completion before any test episode starts.

One test run. Resuming from checkpoint after a crash or kill is not a re-touch; the checkpoint must not be inspected for test outcomes (per-episode labels, deltas, partial AUCs) before the run completes.
Progress logging during the test run is limited to episode counts.

No change to code, config, models, or labels after the first test episode. A discovered bug means a new versioned precommit (nq_dense_precommit_v2.json) that states the bug, and the original result is still disclosed.

artifacts.script: scripts/43_nq_dense_retrieval_full_scale.py (to be written; NQ analogue of scripts/36)

compute_estimate: 2,852 episodes; ~7.5h at TripClick's observed ~9.5s/episode, after scripts/41 finishes. Must not overlap any other pool job.
